entities.summary: Harald Nørregaard was a Norwegian supreme court advocate (høyesterettsadvokat), i.e. a lawyer with the right to appear before the Supreme Court of Norway. He founded the law firm now known as Advokatfirmaet Hjort in 1893 in Christiania, and was Chairman of the Norwegian Bar Association from 1904 to 1907. He was also one of Edvard Munch's closest friends since adolescence, adviser and lawyer. He owned several of Munch's most famous paintings. He was married to Aase Nørregaard née Carlsen (1869–1908), a painter and a close friend of Munch, and secondly to Marit Liv Nørregaard née Tillier (1885–1981), who was also a painter.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a lawyer and close friend of Edvard Munch, Harald Nørregaard played a significant role in promoting Norwegian art and culture during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. His ownership of Munch's paintings helped to establish the artist's reputation internationally.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a close friend and lawyer of Edvard Munch, Harald Nørregaard played a significant role in preserving and promoting Munch's artwork after his death. He owned several of Munch's most famous paintings, ensuring their legacy and contributing to the artist's posthumous recognition.
